newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Moldova's Snegur urges Russian troop withdrawal.
newsitem.headline: Moldova's Snegur urges Russian troop withdrawal.

text.p: Moldova's ousted President Mircea Snegur on Tuesday demanded the removal of Russian troops from his former Soviet republic in what was likely to be his last major speech on the international stage.
Snegur lost a run-off vote in a presidential election on Sunday to Petru Luchinschi, a former leading communist.

He used his address to leaders of more than 50 countries at the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) summit in Lisbon to criticise the presence of Russian troops in Moldova's troubled eastern province of Dnestr.

"Being a neutral state as enshrined in the constitution, the Republic of Moldova cannot accept foreign military presence on its territory," Snegur told the summit, which groups the United States and Canada with all European states.
The Russian-speaking Dnestr region broke away from Moldova in 1990, saying it feared the government of newly independent Moldova wanted to unite with Romania.

The move provoked fierce fighting in 1992 between Moldovan security forces and Dnestr rebels. The warring factions agreed a ceasefire in August 1992 using Moldovan, Russian and Denestr forces to keep the peace.
But Moldova opposes the continued presence of around 6,000 Russian troops who helped keep the peace after the clashes.

"We consider it important that the withdrawal of the Russian troops from the territory of the Republic of Moldova be fulfilled on the basis of the principles of the international law and the pertinent OSCE principles," Snegur said.
Moldova said Russia was holding up the withdrawal of troops by failing to complete internal procedures.
"The situation becomes more alarming because of the numerous hostile decisions of the Russian Duma regarding this problem," Snegur added.

OSCE sources said Moldova had demanded that a final summit document include a clause calling for a quick withdrawal of Russian troops. The Moldovan demand was still being discussed shortly before the scheduled end of the summit, they said.
